invariants.requirement: Valid credentials issue a bearer access token, a revocable refresh token, explicit lifetimes and a public identity without password material.
Unknown identities, wrong passwords and unavailable accounts are rejected with the same public AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS response.
A protected profile endpoint requires a valid access token and returns public identity data without authentication secrets.
Refresh rotates the refresh token, rejects invalid, expired, revoked or already-used tokens and never returns a token hash.
Logout is non-revealing and idempotent and revokes the submitted valid refresh session before it can be refreshed again.
Refresh secrets are stored only as one-way fingerprints and password, token and hash material never appears in public responses.
Credential and refresh exchanges are rate-limited without weakening the Platform Baseline error contract.
Authentication declares and emits business audit events for login success/failure, refresh success/failure and logout through the baseline audit port without recording secrets.
Login establishes an authenticated session while keeping access and refresh tokens outside the public UI state and response surface.
The access token lives only in transient memory, and the refresh token in the most protected store the platform actually offers, reached through a replaceable seam rather than a hard-coded API.
Session restoration and a 401 trigger one coalesced refresh and at most one retry; a failed refresh purges the local session.
Logout requests remote revocation when a refresh token exists and always purges the local session even when the authority is unavailable.
Authentication failures are generic, correlation-aware where available and never expose credentials or token values.

A state-changing authentication operation cannot be triggered by a third-party origin, and any ambient credential the runtime relies on is unreadable by page scripts. A runtime with a server surface satisfies this with same-origin and CSRF validation over HttpOnly cookies; a runtime without one satisfies it by holding no ambient credential at all.
The mobile refresh session is persisted only through the secure-storage abstraction while the access token remains memory-only.
